title: The Number of Beautiful Subsets
summary: Given an array of positive integers and a positive integer k, determine the count of non-empty subsets that do not include any two elements with an absolute difference of k.
statement: Given an array of positive integers and a positive integer k, determine the count of non-empty subsets that do not include any two elements with an absolute difference of k. A subset is formed by removing zero or more elements from the original array, and subsets are considered distinct based on the indices of the elements removed.
constraints: A subset is beautiful when no selected pair has absolute difference k.
Equal values at different indices remain distinct choices.
hints: Backtrack over each index with skip and take branches.
Track frequencies of values currently selected.
Take value x only when neither x-k nor x+k is present, then undo its frequency after recursion.
The traversal enumerates every index subset once, and the frequency condition is exactly the forbidden-difference rule; subtract the empty subset.
editorial: The traversal enumerates every index subset once, and the frequency condition is exactly the forbidden-difference rule; subtract the empty subset.

tests.explanation: The valid nonempty subsets are each singleton and {2,6}, giving four.
The sole singleton contains no pair, so it is beautiful.
